matrix.description: 默认环境，不加载额外插件，用于观察原生 DSH 能力。

session.assistantText:
I'll dispatch one small executor on a role and read back the route it actually resolved to.
**Goal.** Confirm which model route pstack picks for a role with no model line of its own, by dispatching one small executor and reading back what it resolved to.

**What ran.** A single read-only child (`general` agent preset) was spawned on the role `reflect tooling`, with `roleIndex` null since the role is a single shape. Task was a one-command listing of the workspace top level plus a self-report of its own route.

**Route used.** The dispatch resolved to `inherit-parent`. The diagnostic explains why. The role has no line in the pstack models config, so it inherits the parent route rather than picking a role-specific model.

**Evidence from the child.** It reports its own route as `workbuddy/minimax-m3.1-flash`, which maps to the advertised route `magpie/workbuddy/minimax-m3.1-flash`. That is the same model the parent session runs on, so inheritance held. The reasoning effort is not exposed in the child's runtime context. The route advertises `off`, `low`, `high`, `max` with default `high`, so `high` is likely effective, but that is inference from the route default rather than a runtime read.

**One side finding worth acting on.** The `deepseek-official` provider advertises no models at all. Any role or config line naming a route under that provider cannot resolve to a live model, while the `magpie` and `deepseek-account` routes resolve normally. That is a real config gap, not a code defect, and it would silently affect any role pointed there.

**Impact for the maintainer.** The inheritance rule is confirmed working for unconfigured roles. The fix, if you want one, is to add a line for `reflect tooling` in the pstack models config, and to either populate `deepseek-official` or repoint the roles that use it.
